title: Work permit application (Form I-765): documents needed
use_when: Use when the client is applying for an initial, renewal or replacement Employment Authorization Document on Form I-765 under (c)(9), (c)(8), (a)(12)/(c)(19), (c)(33), (c)(3) or (c)(26); use the I-485 family list for the green card application itself.
note: Based on the Form I-765 Instructions (edition 08/21/25), which USCIS says on the form page (last reviewed/updated 11/24/2026) it continues to accept after the Nov. 16, 2026 court order, while not accepting the 09/15/26 edition until further notice. Only the six listed eligibility categories are covered; the list does not decide eligibility, the asylum EAD clock, or filing deadlines, and TPS, DACA and OPT filings also follow the I-821, I-821D and DSO/SEVIS steps.

situations.first-ead: Is this the client's first EAD (never issued one before)?
situations.prior-ead: Has the client been issued an EAD before?
situations.c9: Is the client applying under (c)(9) because a Form I-485 adjustment application is pending?
situations.c8: Is the client applying under (c)(8) because an asylum application (Form I-589) is pending?
situations.tps: Is the client applying under (a)(12) or (c)(19) as a TPS applicant or beneficiary?
situations.daca: Is the client applying under (c)(33) with a DACA request (Form I-821D)?
situations.opt: Is the client an F-1 student applying for pre- or post-completion OPT under (c)(3)(A) or (c)(3)(B)?
situations.stem-opt: Is the client an F-1 student applying for the 24-month STEM OPT extension under (c)(3)(C)?
situations.h4: Is the client the H-4 spouse of an H-1B worker applying under (c)(26)?
situations.arrests: Has the client (a (c)(8) applicant) ever been arrested for or convicted of any crime?
situations.foreign-language: Are any documents in a language other than English?

items.label: Two identical color passport-style photos taken recently
items.detail: 2 by 2 inches, full face, white to off-white background, thin glossy paper, unmounted and unretouched; head 1 to 1 3/8 inches; name and A-Number lightly printed on the back. Required Documentation, 3.C.

items.label: Copy of your I-94 arrival record, passport, or other travel document
items.detail: At least one of: Form I-94 (front and back), printout of the electronic I-94 from cbp.gov/i94, passport, or other travel document. Not required for (c)(9) applicants. Required Documentation, 3.A. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Copy of your last work permit (front and back)
items.detail: Required Documentation, 3.B. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Copy of a government-issued photo ID
items.detail: Such as a passport showing picture, name and date of birth; a birth certificate with photo ID; a foreign consular visa; or a national ID with photo and/or fingerprint. Must clearly show facial features and biographic details. (c)(33) applicants need nothing beyond the identity documents filed with Form I-821D. Required Documentation, 3.B. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Full English translation of every foreign-language document
items.detail: With the translator's certification that it is complete and accurate and that they are competent to translate.

items.label: Copy of the Form I-485 receipt notice, or other proof the I-485 is pending
items.detail: Not needed if the I-765 is filed together with the I-485. If the I-485 is before an immigration court (EOIR), proof the client is in proceedings, that the I-485 was properly filed with the court, and that it remains pending. Asylees and refugees file under (a)(5) or (a)(3), not (c)(9).

items.label: Proof the asylum application was filed with USCIS
items.detail: Copy of the USCIS Acknowledgement of Receipt and the Asylum Interview Notice (scheduling, rescheduling or cancelling), the Form I-797C biometrics appointment notice, or other evidence of filing. Special Filing Instructions (c)(8), item 4.A.

items.label: Proof the asylum application was lodged or filed with the immigration court, if filed there
items.detail: Copy of the acknowledgement of receipt or other available evidence. Item 4.B. If an immigration judge denied asylum after the 180-day clock ran: evidence of a timely, still-pending BIA appeal (and court of appeals petition, if any). If remanded: the BIA remand order and evidence the claim is still under review. Items 4.C-4.D.

items.label: Recommended Approval notice from the asylum office, if received
items.detail: Lets the client file immediately without waiting 150 days.

items.label: Certified copies of all arrest reports, court dispositions and sentencing documents
items.detail: Required for initial and renewal (c)(8) applications; include information on every conviction. Special Filing Instructions (c)(8), item 4.E.

items.label: Form I-821, or proof USCIS received or approved the initial or re-registration I-821
items.detail: Follow the most recent TPS Federal Register notice for the client's country.

items.label: Evidence of nationality and identity as the Form I-821 instructions require
items.detail: Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Immigration judge or BIA order granting TPS, if TPS was granted in court
items.detail: For a first EAD or first re-registration; for example the I-821 the judge or BIA approved.

items.label: For re-registration: a letter saying the filing is for TPS re-registration and a copy of the last TPS document
items.detail: Copy front and back of the last available TPS document (for example an EAD, I-94, passport, travel document, or I-797 notice). For a lost, stolen or damaged TPS EAD: the TPS approval notice, or the prior I-797 for the I-821 if still pending. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Form I-821D, Consideration of Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals, filed together
Form I-765WS worksheet showing income, expenses and assets
items.detail: Shows economic necessity to work. Supporting evidence is optional; other household members' finances are not needed. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Form I-20 endorsed by the school's DSO
items.detail: Required for pre-completion OPT (c)(3)(A). For post-completion and STEM OPT the DSO must enter the recommendation in SEVIS first; file within 30 days (post-completion) or 60 days (STEM) of that recommendation.

items.label: Proof of full-time enrollment for one full academic year at an SEVP-approved school
items.detail: For pre-completion OPT (c)(3)(A).

items.label: All previously used SEVIS numbers and proof of any earlier CPT or OPT, with the academic level of each
items.detail: For (c)(3)(A) and (c)(3)(B); post-completion applicants list these in Part 6.

items.label: Evidence the degree is on the STEM Designated Degree Program List
items.detail: If based on a previously earned STEM degree, also a copy of that degree and evidence the school is currently accredited by the Department of Education and SEVP-certified.

items.label: STEM employer's name as listed in E-Verify and its E-Verify company ID number
items.detail: Or E-Verify Client Company ID. Also degree level and major. Part 2, Items 28.a-28.c.

sections.name: H-4 spouse of an H-1B worker (c)(26)

items.label: Proof of current H-4 status
items.detail: Copy of the current I-797 for Form I-539, or the I-94 showing H-4 admission or most recent approved extension.

items.label: Copy of the marriage certificate
items.detail: If unavailable, USCIS will consider secondary evidence of the relationship.

items.label: Spouse's I-140 approval notice, or proof the spouse got an AC21 106(a)/(b) extension
items.detail: Approved I-140: copy of the spouse's I-797 for Form I-140. AC21: copies of the spouse's passports, prior I-94s, and current and prior I-797s for Form I-129, plus evidence of the basis for the extension. Send through the secure portal, never by plain email.

items.label: Receipt number of the spouse's most recent Form I-129 notice (I-797)
items.detail: Part 2, Item 29.
